guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul Standard ("Greeny", ex-Peter Green)
models: Gibson Les Paul Standard ("Greeny", ex-Peter Green)
guitar.notes: Confirmed and refined — Gary Moore's 1959 Les Paul "Greeny" (previously owned by Peter Green) is one of the most famous guitars in blues-rock history.

tone.target: sustained singing blues lead with warm neck humbucker
tone.profile: sustained singing blues lead with warm neck humbucker
tone.summary: A warm, sustained blues lead tone using a smooth overdrive and classic British amp voicing (UK 45) combined with plate reverb for vocal sustain.

rig.name: Gary Moore - Still Got The Blues - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide slight compression for sustained notes and even dynamics.
Smooth tube overdrive to emulate the warm lead tone and sustain.
Placeholder/Optional: Used for slight grit if Blues OD isn't enough. Kept inactive to prioritize smooth tone.
blocks.gap: The primary gain is handled by the Blues OD, so this is kept off but available for extra bite.

blocks.purpose: Simulate a classic British lead amp voicing (Marshall-like) for the blues sound.
Provide a classic British cabinet sound matching the UK 45 amp.
Enhance the vocal midrange frequencies crucial for blues lead tone.
Add subtle vibrato effect to enhance the singing lead quality.
blocks.gap: A dedicated Vibrato module would be ideal, but Tremolo is used for controlled pitch modulation.

blocks.purpose: Provide long, warm sustain and a sense of space (vocal reverb).
Add subtle rhythmic echo without distracting from the lead melody.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR for better cabinet realism to match the vintage Les Paul/Marshall tone.

proposals.reason: Enhance classic blues warmth and definition missing from generic IR.
